note: Adapted from Sands 1965 (a revision of the Ethiopian Nasutitermitinae), original in English. Sands places N. konduensis, N. putidus, N. aethiops, N. dulcis and N. chapini as new synonyms of this species (syn. n.); the alate was previously undescribed, and the account of this species is based on the type series from Basongo, Congo, and on several lots. Measurements such as soldier head depth and postmentum length were cut off in the OCR and are not recorded.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier head capsule orange-yellow to iron-orange, nasus iron-coloured to chestnut-brown with a reddish apex; head capsule in dorsal view short-oval to nearly circular, nasus conical, abruptly narrowing near the apex; in lateral view distinctly concave, often with a small hump at the base of the nasus; posterior part of the vertex raised and rounded. Nasus (measured from the posterior margin of the antennal socket) shorter than the rest of the head capsule; nasal cone angle 12—15 degrees; cephalic pilosity consisting of a pair on each side of the vertex (not always present), a distinctly hairy nasus apex and a few hairs on the anterior margin of the postmentum, the rest of the postmentum surface with very rarely 1—2 small hairs. The alate differs from most species in its larger size; for the distinction from N. chrysopleura see that species.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark sepia-brown; postclypeus and antennae sepia-brown, labrum brown; pronotum and abdominal tergites dark sepia-brown; meso- and metanotal tergites and the sides of the sternites sepia-brown, legs and middle of the sternites yellowish brown; wing membrane pale translucent sepia-brown, subcosta and radial sector yellowish brown, the posterior margin of the radial sector lined with dark brown, the remaining veins brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule behind the compound eyes evenly rounded, less than a semicircle; fontanelle small, pale, weakly forked in front; compound eyes moderately projecting relative to their own diameter, slightly angular-oval, moderately large relative to head width, W/E index 2.9—3.1; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by 1/2 to 3/4 of their own least diameter; postclypeus weakly raised, 3.6 times as wide as long, anterior margin slightly wavy, posterior margin convex, almost straight in the middle and curved toward the outer corners; antennae 15-segmented, segment 2 longer than segment 4, segment 4 longer than segment 5, segment 5 longer than segment 3. Female cercus about as long as wide at its base. Measurements (mm, 8 individuals, 2 localities): head width (including compound eyes) 1.33—1.40; maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.44—0.46 (mean 0.45); ocellus 0.11—0.13×0.15—0.18 (mean 0.12×0.16); ocellus to compound eye 0.08—0.10 (mean 0.08); pronotum width 1.10—1.17 (mean 1.14); pronotum length 0.66—0.74 (mean 0.71); hind tibia length 1.58—1.68 (mean 1.63); fore wing length 11.50—12.40 (mean 11.90). Morphotype: Abidjan, Ivory Coast, November 1949 (month 11) (R. Geigy), female morphotype deposited in the American Museum of Natural History.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule orange-yellow to iron-orange, nasus iron-coloured to chestnut-brown with a reddish apex; pronotum and antennae as in the head capsule; abdominal tergites and legs yellow, sternites pale yellow. Head capsule in dorsal view short-oval to circular, nasus conical, abruptly narrowing near the apex; in lateral view distinctly concave, often with a small hump at the base of the nasus, the posterior part of the head raised and rounded. Nasus shorter than the rest of the head capsule (measured from the posterior margin of the antennal socket, except in the smallest individuals); nasal cone angle 12—15 degrees; postmentum moderately and evenly raised; antennae 12—14-segmented, mostly 13-segmented, segments 2 and 4 subequal in length and shorter than segment 5, segment 3 longer than segment 5. Cephalic pilosity: a pair on each side of the vertex (not always present), a distinctly hairy nasus apex, a few hairs on the anterior margin of the postmentum, the rest of the postmentum surface with very rarely 1—2 minute hairs, and usually a few hairs on the vertex. Abdominal tergites with very short scattered hairs, the posterior margins of the last 4 segments with 4 rows of longer hairs; sternites with scattered short hairs, the posterior margin of each segment with 6 long hairs. Measurements (mm, 39 individuals, 9 localities): head length (to the nasus apex) 1.43—1.75 (mean 1.59); head width 0.85—1.13 (mean 0.98).
